title: Tiwanaku at its height
description: The city near Lake Titicaca, with its stone temples and gateways, is the centre of a state that dominates the southern Andes.

title: Incallajta built
description: The Inca ruler Túpac Yupanqui builds a fortress on the eastern edge of the empire after conquering the region.

title: La Plata founded
description: Pedro de Anzúrez founds the city of La Plata, later called Chuquisaca and Sucre.

title: Silver found at Potosí
description: The discovery of silver in the Cerro Rico begins a mining boom that supplies much of the world's silver.

title: La Paz founded
description: Alonso de Mendoza founds Nuestra Señora de La Paz at Laja, and the city moves to its present valley days later.

title: Audiencia of Charcas
description: Philip II creates a high court at La Plata whose district later becomes the territory of Bolivia.

title: Santa Cruz de la Sierra founded
place: Santa Cruz la Vieja, near San José de Chiquitos
description: Ñuflo de Chaves founds the first Spanish town in the eastern lowlands, later moved west to its present site.

title: Potosí mita
description: Viceroy Francisco de Toledo organises the forced labour draft that sends Andean villagers to the silver mines.

title: University of San Francisco Xavier founded
description: The Jesuits found a university at La Plata that later trains many leaders of South American independence.

title: Siege of La Paz
polity: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
description: An Aymara army under Túpac Katari besieges La Paz for months before Spanish troops break the siege.

title: Chuquisaca Revolution
polity: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
description: Residents of Chuquisaca depose the president of the Audiencia, an early step towards independence in Spanish America.

title: Declaration of independence
description: An assembly of the provinces of Upper Peru declares independence and names the new state after Bolívar.

title: Peru–Bolivian Confederation
description: The Bolivian president Andrés de Santa Cruz decrees a confederation of Bolivia with North and South Peru, which lasts three years.

title: Battle of Ingavi
description: The Bolivian army defeats a Peruvian invasion and kills President Gamarra, securing Bolivia's independence.

title: Battle of Tacna
description: Chile defeats the allied Peruvian and Bolivian armies, after which Bolivia takes no further part in the War of the Pacific.

title: Federal War
description: Liberals from La Paz defeat the Conservative government of Sucre, and the seat of government moves to La Paz.

title: Treaty of Petrópolis
description: Bolivia cedes the rubber-rich territory of Acre to Brazil in return for money and a railway.

title: Peace treaty with Chile
description: Bolivia accepts the loss of its Pacific coast to Chile, leaving the country landlocked.

title: Chaco War
description: Bolivia loses most of the Chaco to Paraguay in a war that costs it tens of thousands of dead and ends with its army holding the line at Villamontes.

title: National Revolution
description: A rising of the MNR party, miners and police defeats the army and brings universal suffrage and nationalisation of the tin mines.

title: Agrarian reform
description: A decree signed at Ucureña breaks up the large estates of the highlands and gives land to indigenous peasants.

title: Banzer's coup
description: Colonel Hugo Banzer overthrows the left-wing government of Juan José Torres and rules for seven years.

title: Democracy restored
description: Hernán Siles Zuazo takes office as president, ending eighteen years of mostly military rule.

title: Decree 21060
description: President Víctor Paz Estenssoro ends hyperinflation with a decree that opens the economy and cuts the state sector.

title: Cochabamba Water War
description: Protests force the government to cancel the privatisation of the city's water supply.

title: Gas War
description: President Gonzalo Sánchez de Lozada resigns after weeks of protests over gas exports in which dozens of people are killed.

title: Evo Morales elected
description: Evo Morales wins the presidency with an outright majority, the first indigenous president of Bolivia.

title: New constitution
description: Voters approve a constitution that defines Bolivia as a plurinational state.

title: Morales resigns
description: Evo Morales resigns after a disputed election, weeks of protests and a call from the armed forces to step down.
